title: Written review: Computer Systems Servicing
description: A summary of the key points from every category, followed by a mixed review quiz to check you are ready for an assessment.
objectives: Recall the key facts from each area of the library.
Check your readiness with a mixed quiz.
Find the lessons to revisit for any weak area.

safety.text: Safety questions appear in every CSS assessment. Review "Electrical safety and ESD precautions" first.

steps.title: Safety and hardware
steps.body:
- Unplug, drain power, wear a grounded wrist strap; never open a PSU.
- RAM is volatile working memory; storage keeps data.
- The PSU turns 220 V AC into +12 V, +5 V and +3.3 V DC.
- Every motherboard needs the 24-pin ATX and 8-pin CPU cables.

steps.title: Assembly and troubleshooting
steps.body:
- Never force a part: check the notch, key or latch.
- The six troubleshooting steps: identify, theory, test, plan and fix, verify, document.
- Change one thing at a time. Test the simplest causes first.
- No display: check input, cable, card vs board, RAM, minimal configuration.

steps.title: Windows
steps.body:
- Windows 11 needs TPM 2.0, UEFI with Secure Boot, 4 GB RAM and 64 GB storage.
- Repairs from least destructive: Startup Repair, System Restore, Safe Mode, DISM then SFC, and Reset this PC last.
- Only genuine licences; never activators.

steps.title: Networking
steps.body:
- IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS.
- 169.254.x.x means DHCP failed.
- T568B: white-orange, orange, white-green, blue, white-blue, green, white-brown, brown.
- Ping outward: 127.0.0.1, gateway, 8.8.8.8, a name.

steps.title: Printers, maintenance and tools
steps.body:
- Stuck queue: restart the Print Spooler. Laser steps: processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning.
- Hold fans still under compressed air; no household vacuums inside.
- Don't defragment SSDs. Back up with 3-2-1.
- ATX tolerance ±5% (+12 V: 11.40–12.60 V). Yellow +12 V, red +5 V, orange +3.3 V.

steps.title: Take the review quiz
steps.body: Answer the quiz without looking back. For each question you miss, open that topic's lesson in the library and review it, then try again.

expectedResults: You score 80% or more on the review quiz.
You know which lessons to revisit for any question you missed.

commonMistakes.why: Practical assessments ask you to apply the knowledge to a real fault.
commonMistakes.fix: For each fact, ask yourself what would happen on a real computer if you got it wrong.
